q: 1. A document containing detailed description of all items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: The Schedule of Rates (SOR) is a list containing the description of items and their sanctioned rates, used as a reference for preparing estimates.

q: 2. The essential requirements to prepare a good estimate are
options: a full dimensioned drawing to scale
explain: To prepare an accurate estimate, one needs the dimensions (drawings), the quality of work (specifications), and the cost per unit (SOR).

q: 3. No deductions are made in the masonry for the openings if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Per IS codes, deductions are not required for small openings (like ventilation or pipe holes) up to 0.1 square meters in area.

q: 4. The quantity for expansion joint in buildings is worked out in
explain: Expansion joints are typically measured by their length in running meters (m).

q: 5. The rate of an item of work depends on
explain: The unit rate is influenced by the quality of materials, the ratio of the mix (like 1:3 vs 1:6 mortar), and the complexity of the work description.

q: 6. For electric wiring such as fan, light, plug, the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in kw
total length of wiring in metres.
explain: Internal electrical wiring is generally estimated by counting the 'number of points' (light point, fan point, etc.).

q: 7. End lap provided in asbestos cement sheets is equal to
explain: For normal slopes, an end lap (vertical overlap) of 15 cm is the standard requirement.

q: 8. The unit of measurement of terrazzo or marble or tile flooring is
explain: Flooring is a surface treatment and is measured by the total area covered in square metres (m²).

q: 9. The measurement is made in square metre in case of
explain: Concrete foundation and RCC work are measured in cubic metres (m³), and hollow block walls are also typically measured in m³ (unless very thin).

q: 10. The area is measured correct to the nearest
explain: In estimation, all area measurements are recorded to two decimal places, i.e., 0.01 square metres.

q: 11. The 'center line method' is specially adopted for estimating
explain: The centerline method is the fastest way to estimate quantities for buildings with uniform cross-sections, especially those with circular or polygonal plans.

q: 12. The trap which is provide to disconnect the house drain from the street sewer is called
explain: All these terms refer to the Intercepting Trap located at the last point of the house drainage system before it joins the public sewer.

q: 13. Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
options: Bottom of P trap W. C.
Top of P trap W. C.
explain: Anti-siphonage pipes are connected to the top of the P-trap to prevent the water seal from being sucked out by atmospheric pressure changes.

q: 14. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of embankment, side slope S : 1... the area of cross-section is
explain: Area of a trapezoidal embankment section = Area of central rectangle (B*d) + Area of two side triangles (2 * 1/2 * Sd * d) = Bd + Sd².

q: 15. If the formation level... has a uniform gradient... and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope...
explain: Earthwork volume can be calculated using any of these mathematical methods depending on the required accuracy and ground profile.

q: 16. To account for the corrugations, the plain area of the semi-corrugated asbestos sheet is increased (for white washing)
explain: For corrugated surfaces, the flat area is increased by a percentage (10% for semi-corrugated, 20% for corrugated) to account for the actual surface area being painted/washed.

q: 17. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion... is
explain: In surveying, chainage is recorded as 'Chain + Links'. For 30m intervals, 15 chains (if using 20m chain) or specific local link counts are used to designate the station.

q: 18. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: The payment for explosives used in blasting is often calculated by weight (kg), though the excavation itself is usually cu m. In this context, the explosive material/effort is kg.

q: 19. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: Supervision or work-charged establishment charges generally range from 5% to 10% to cover the cost of technical staff employed during construction.

q: 20. The useful part of livable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area is the net usable area within the walls of a building where a carpet can be laid, excluding the thickness of inner walls, balconies, and common areas.

q: 21. Thickness of plastering is usually
explain: Standard plastering for internal brick walls is usually 12 mm thick. Ceiling plaster is typically 6 mm, and external plaster is 18-20 mm.

q: 22. In a galvanized corrugated iron sheet the pitch (center to center distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: The standard pitch for corrugations in GI sheets used in roofing is typically 75 mm (or 3 inches).

q: 23. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: A P-trap outlet is designed with a specific downward slope (usually around 14 degrees) to ensure efficient drainage and maintain the water seal.

q: 24. The concrete work for the following parts of the building of specified thickness is measured in square metres
explain: Damp Proof Course (D.P.C.) is measured in square metres because it is a thin layer with a specified thickness. Roof slabs and floors are typically measured in cubic metres unless they are very thin, but D.P.C. is the most standard answer here.

q: 25. While submitting a tender the contractor is required to deposit some amount with the department, as guarantee of the tender known as
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is a small percentage (usually 1-2%) of the estimated cost paid by the bidder to show interest and prevent frivolous bidding.

q: 26. Provisional sum provided in the bill of quantities is paid to the contractor on the basis of:
explain: A provisional sum is an allowance for work that cannot be fully detailed at the time of tender; it is usually settled based on the actual cost incurred.

q: 27. The weight of water per cubic foot is:
explain: One cubic foot of water weighs approximately 62.4 lbs, which converts to roughly 28.31 kgf (rounded to 28.363 in some technical tables).

q: 28. One mile is 1.625km, also it is:
explain: In the Imperial system, 1 mile is exactly equal to 8 furlongs (each furlong being 220 yards).

q: 29. In the detailed estimate the volumes are worked out to the nearest
explain: According to IS 1200, quantities of volume are generally rounded to the nearest 0.01 cubic meter.

q: 30. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S : 1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: The cross-sectional area consists of a central rectangle (B × d) and two side triangles (each 1/2 × Sd × d), totaling Bd + Sd².

q: 31. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measures in sq. m
plastering is measures in sq. m
striking is measures in sq. m
explain: All surface-finishing works like pointing, plastering, and formwork striking are measured by area (m²).

q: 32. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm is
explain: Surface excavation or 'surface dressing' not exceeding 30 cm in depth is measured in square meters (m²).

q: 33. One hectare-meter represent a volume of
explain: 1 Hectare = 10,000 m². Therefore, 1 Hectare-meter = 10,000 m² * 1 m = 10,000 m³.

q: 34. How many kilo-liters are there in one cubic meter?
explain: 1 m³ = 1000 liters. Since 1000 liters = 1 kilo-liter (kL), then 1 m³ = 1 kL.

q: 35. Carpet area does not include the area of
options: the walls along with doors and other openings
explain: Carpet area is the net usable floor area excluding walls, circulation areas (corridors), and sanitary blocks.

q: 36. In what units are the quantities for the frames of doors and windows computed
explain: Door and window frames (Chaukhats) are made of timber and are measured by their total volume in cubic meters (m³).

q: 37. The correct relationship between rise, R and tread, T is
explain: A standard rule of thumb for comfortable stair design is that twice the rise plus the tread (in mm) should equal approximately 600 mm (2R + T = 600).

q: 38. The unit of measurement of roofing (each and every detail specified) is
explain: Roofing work (sheets, tiles, or slabs) is measured by the net planar area covered, expressed in square meters (m²).

q: 39. The unit of measurement of railing is ............
explain: Railings for stairs, balconies, or corridors are typically measured in running meters (per m) as the height is usually standard, making the length the primary variable.

q: 40. The quantity of cement concrete damp-proofing course is measured in terms of ............
explain: Damp-proofing course (DPC) has a specified thickness; therefore, it is measured by area in square meters (m2).

q: 41. The areas of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S : 1 and length L is ............
explain: Using Pythagoras theorem for the slope length (sqrt(d^2 + (sd)^2)) and multiplying by the length (L), the formula simplifies to L * d * sqrt(1 + s^2).

q: 42. The essential requirements to prepare a good estimate are ............
options: a full dimensioned drawing to scale
explain: A comprehensive estimate requires geometric data (drawings), quality standards (specifications), and unit costs (schedule of rates).

q: 43. The unit of measurement of earth in filling ............
explain: Earthwork, whether for excavation or filling, is a volumetric task and is measured in cubic meters (m3).

q: 44. The R.C.C. work in beam, slab and lintel is measured in ............
explain: Standard structural R.C.C. components like beams and slabs are calculated by their total volume in cubic meters (m3).

q: 45. If the bearing is not specified for the lintel, in the estimation it is usually taken as ............
options: thickness of lintel subjected to minimum value of 12 cm
3/4 of lintel thickness or 12 cm whichever is large
explain: If not specified, the end bearing of a lintel should be equal to the thickness of the lintel or 12cm, whichever is greater (common convention is often cited as 3/4 to full thickness).

q: 46. The unit of measurement of holdfast is ............
explain: Holdfasts are iron fixtures, and like most structural steel or iron items, they are measured by weight in kilograms (kg) or quintals.

q: 47. The document unit of measurement of binding wire in R.C.C. work is measured in ............
explain: Binding wire is typically calculated as a percentage of steel weight or measured in weight units like quintals (100 kg).

q: 48. The unit of measurement of jungle clearance including uprooting vegetation, shrubs, grass etc ............
explain: Clearing a site of surface vegetation is measured by the area cleared, in m2.

q: 49. The unit of measurement of supply of sand, surkhi, brick blast is ............
explain: Bulk construction materials like sand and surkhi are supplied and measured by volume in cubic meters (m3).
